Definition: to fly; also (by implication of dimness) to faint (from the darkness of swooning)
BiblicalUsage: On the fifth day God said, let the waters bring forth abundantly, and fowl that may fly above the earth, and the law forbids making the likeness of any winged fowl that flies in the air.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe flight is one of God's first gifts to His creatures: He made the air a road for birds before He gave men any road at all, and then warned us not to worship the likeness of what He made.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
